assumptions: this subdomain sits under creator_craft_and_content_production and models concrete visual-production work units
scope centers on lighting and camera, with adjacent audio and edit work units that gate deliverable quality
no observed dataset or benchmark is supplied; all numbers are heuristic priors
nodes are bounded so one heavy reasoning session can complete, validate, and hand off each step
exclusions: screenwriting and narrative scripting beyond shot purpose
distribution, marketing, and audience analytics after delivery
motion graphics, VFX, and 3D rendering pipelines
business and contracting aspects of production

competency_questions.question: What must the footage show, for whom, and what single viewer outcome should it produce?
How are aperture, shutter, and ISO set to reach correct exposure for the intended look?
What frame rate and shutter give the intended motion cadence without flicker?
How is white balance and source color temperature managed so neutrals read true?
How are lens, focal length, depth of field, and framing chosen for the shot?
How is the image composed so the subject reads clearly and intentionally?
How is three-point and shaped lighting built from key, fill, and backlight?
How is available daylight read and shaped, and the location controlled, before lighting?
How is camera support and movement planned and coverage guaranteed for the edit?
How is clean dialogue and ambience captured so audio does not sink the visuals?
How is exposure and focus verified objectively rather than judged by eye?
How are footage and audio edited, graded, and QC-checked into a delivered master?

glossary.definition: the interlocked relationship of aperture, shutter speed, and ISO that sets brightness and look
the camera setting that makes neutral tones render neutral under a given light color
the warm-to-cool color of a light source measured in kelvin
the lens property that sets field of view and perspective compression
the range of distance that appears acceptably sharp in the frame
a framing guide placing key elements on thirds lines for balance
a setup using key, fill, and backlight to model and separate the subject
the brightness ratio between key and fill that sets shadow depth and mood
whether light is hard or soft, set by source size and diffusion
a scope showing luminance distribution used to verify exposure
the post process of balancing and stylizing footage color and contrast
setting audio levels so signal is strong but never clips

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established visual-production literature (Stockman, How to Shoot Video That Doesn't Suck; Brown, Cinematography: Theory and Practice; Freeman, The Photographer's Eye) and standard camera, lighting, audio, and post practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix what the footage must show, for whom, and the single intended viewer outcome before any camera or light is set.
contradictors: shooter who rolls with no plan

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the deliverable, platform, or creative intent changes

pros.claim: every camera and light choice inherits one clear goal
pros.example: a vertical social cut needs different framing than a 16:9 interview

cons.claim: a wrong goal misdirects the whole shoot
cons.example: lighting a moody scene the client wanted bright

failure_modes: goal stated as a topic not an outcome
platform or aspect assumed wrong
acceptance_tests: purpose is one sentence naming a viewer outcome
deliverable spec names platform and aspect

nodes.definition: Set aperture, shutter speed, and ISO together to reach correct brightness while controlling motion blur, depth, and noise.
contradictors: auto-everything shooter

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when lighting, lens, or motion requirements change

pros.claim: one framework links brightness to look
pros.example: open the aperture for shallow depth then drop ISO to hold noise

cons.claim: a wrong leg of the triangle is hard to fix later
cons.example: high ISO bakes noise that no grade removes

failure_modes: clipped highlights from over-exposure
motion blur from a slow shutter at the wrong frame rate
acceptance_tests: histogram shows no unintended clipping
shutter matches the 180-degree rule for the frame rate
revisit_triggers: frame rate or motion brief changes

nodes.definition: Choose capture frame rate and shutter angle for the intended motion cadence, slow-motion needs, and flicker-free light.
contradictors: shooter ignoring shutter and flicker

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when slow-motion or delivery cadence requirements change

pros.claim: motion cadence and slow-motion are decided deliberately
pros.example: shoot 60fps to retime to smooth slow motion

cons.claim: wrong base rate or shutter causes flicker or judder
cons.example: banding under LED light at the wrong shutter

failure_modes: flicker or banding under artificial light
unusable judder from a frame-rate and shutter mismatch
acceptance_tests: no banding visible under the working lights
frame rate supports the intended retime

nodes.definition: Match camera white balance to the dominant light color temperature so neutrals read true and mixed sources are reconciled.
contradictors: leaves white balance on auto in mixed light

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when light sources or creative warmth intent change

pros.claim: neutrals stay true and grading starts clean
pros.example: setting 3200K under tungsten keeps skin natural

cons.claim: mixed sources produce color casts hard to grade out
cons.example: window daylight plus tungsten splits a face into two tints

failure_modes: green or magenta cast from fluorescent or LED
split color across a mixed-light frame
acceptance_tests: a gray card reads neutral on a scope
mixed sources are gelled or balanced to one reference

nodes.definition: Select focal length and lens to control field of view, perspective compression, and the subject-to-background relationship.
contradictors: always shoots one zoom at one length

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when framing, distance, or perspective intent changes

pros.claim: focal length shapes how the viewer reads space
pros.example: an 85mm flatters a face by compressing the background

cons.claim: a wrong length distorts faces or cramps the frame
cons.example: a 24mm too close enlarges the nose

failure_modes: wide-angle facial distortion
no working room for the chosen length
acceptance_tests: focal length matches the perspective intent
working distance is achievable on location

nodes.definition: Control aperture, distance, and focal length to set how much is sharp, and keep the subject reliably in focus.
contradictors: shoots wide open with no focus discipline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when subject movement or aperture choice changes

pros.claim: separation directs the eye to the subject
pros.example: a shallow depth blurs a busy background

cons.claim: too-shallow focus on a moving subject yields soft takes
cons.example: eyes drift out of focus when the subject leans

failure_modes: soft focus on the subject's eyes
focus hunts during a move
acceptance_tests: the subject's eyes are critically sharp at 100 percent
focus holds through the planned movement

nodes.definition: Arrange subject, headroom, lead space, and balance using rule-of-thirds and related framing principles for clear, intentional images.
contradictors: centers everything with no intent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when aspect, subject, or story emphasis changes

pros.claim: deliberate framing makes images read instantly
pros.example: placing eyes on the upper third gives natural headroom

cons.claim: weak framing buries the subject
cons.example: too much headroom shrinks the subject

failure_modes: subject lost in clutter
cramped or excessive headroom
acceptance_tests: subject placement follows a stated framing intent
headroom and lead space are deliberate

nodes.definition: Place and shape the dominant light to define the subject's form, exposure, and the primary direction of light.
contradictors: lights flat from the camera axis only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when subject blocking or mood intent changes

pros.claim: the key sets form and mood in one decision
pros.example: a 45-degree key carves cheekbones for a dramatic look

cons.claim: a mis-placed key flattens or harshly shadows the face
cons.example: an on-axis key kills all dimensionality

failure_modes: flat lighting with no modeling
harsh unflattering shadow from a bad key angle
acceptance_tests: the key creates intended modeling on the subject
key exposure matches the metered target

nodes.definition: Add or subtract fill to set the key-to-fill contrast ratio that controls shadow depth and overall mood.
contradictors: fills shadows flat by default

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when mood or contrast intent changes

pros.claim: the ratio dials mood from soft to dramatic
pros.example: a 2:1 ratio reads gentle while 8:1 reads moody

cons.claim: over-fill removes all dimensionality
cons.example: flat fill makes a face look like a passport photo

failure_modes: shadows crushed to black with no detail
face flattened by excess fill
acceptance_tests: the key-to-fill ratio matches the mood intent
shadow detail is retained where intended

nodes.definition: Use back or rim light to separate the subject from the background and add depth to the frame.
contradictors: ignores subject and background separation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when background tone or subject distance changes

pros.claim: a rim lifts the subject off the background
pros.example: a hair light separates dark hair from a dark wall

cons.claim: too-hot a backlight blows hair or rims unnaturally
cons.example: a clipped rim looks like a halo

failure_modes: subject merges with the background
blown-out rim or hair light
acceptance_tests: the subject reads as separate from the background
the rim is not clipped on a scope

nodes.definition: Read, shape, and supplement available daylight or practicals to achieve the look without a full lighting kit.
contradictors: fights daylight instead of using it

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when time of day, weather, or location light changes

pros.claim: daylight gives a free, beautiful soft source
pros.example: backlit golden-hour window light flatters skin

cons.claim: available light changes fast and is hard to control
cons.example: clouds drop two stops mid-take

failure_modes: exposure shifts as the sun moves
harsh midday top-light on faces
acceptance_tests: the available-light direction matches the intended look
a shaping plan handles changing daylight

nodes.definition: Match or deliberately mismatch source color temperatures with gels and modifiers to unify or stylize the lighting.
contradictors: mixes color temps with no plan

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when source temps or creative color intent change

pros.claim: gels reconcile mixed sources or add deliberate color
pros.example: a CTB gel on a tungsten lamp matches a daylight window

cons.claim: un-gelled mixed temps fight in the same frame
cons.example: one warm and one cool lamp split the subject

failure_modes: color split across the frame
a gel choice that muddies skin tones
acceptance_tests: sources are unified to one temperature or stylized on purpose
skin tones read as intended after gels

nodes.definition: Choose softboxes, diffusion, bounce, and flags to set whether light is hard or soft and how it falls off.
contradictors: uses bare lamps for everything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when desired light hardness or subject size changes

pros.claim: modifiers control hardness independent of intensity
pros.example: a large softbox wraps soft light around a face

cons.claim: the wrong modifier gives unflattering hard or flat light
cons.example: a bare lamp casts a harsh nose shadow

failure_modes: harsh shadows from an undiffused source
soft light with no direction or shape
acceptance_tests: light hardness matches the intended look
falloff and shadow edge are as planned

nodes.definition: Choose tripod, gimbal, slider, or handheld and plan camera moves for stability and motivated motion.
contradictors: shoots everything shaky handheld

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when movement intent or shooting space changes

pros.claim: stable, motivated moves look intentional and professional
pros.example: a slow slider push adds energy to a static interview

cons.claim: unmotivated shake distracts and signals amateur work
cons.example: jittery handheld on a locked-off interview

failure_modes: unwanted shake or micro-jitter
a move with no narrative motivation
acceptance_tests: footage is stable to the intended degree
each move is motivated by the shot's purpose

nodes.definition: Select and place microphones and set levels so dialogue and ambience are clean, since bad audio sinks good visuals.
contradictors: relies on the on-camera mic only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when location acoustics or dialogue needs change

pros.claim: clean audio is half the perceived quality
pros.example: a lav close to the mouth beats a distant on-camera mic

cons.claim: clipped or noisy audio often cannot be salvaged
cons.example: a peaked level distorts dialogue permanently

failure_modes: clipped or distorted dialogue
room noise or echo overwhelming speech
acceptance_tests: levels peak below clipping with healthy headroom
dialogue is intelligible over the noise floor

nodes.definition: Scout and dress the shooting space to control background clutter, light, color, and acoustics before rolling.
contradictors: shoots in front of whatever is there

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when location availability or background needs change

pros.claim: a controlled background and acoustics prevent on-set problems
pros.example: a quiet room with a clean wall saves audio and framing

cons.claim: a bad location forces compromises in light, sound, and frame
cons.example: a noisy cafe ruins both audio and concentration

failure_modes: distracting clutter behind the subject
uncontrollable noise or light at the location
acceptance_tests: the background is clean or intentionally dressed
light and acoustics at the location are workable

nodes.definition: Use histograms, waveforms, false color, and focus peaking on a monitor to verify exposure and focus objectively while shooting.
contradictors: judges exposure by the rear LCD only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when capture format or exposure target changes

pros.claim: scopes catch clipping and soft focus the eye misses
pros.example: false color flags blown highlights on white shirts

cons.claim: trusting the LCD hides exposure and focus errors
cons.example: a bright LCD fools you into under-exposing

failure_modes: unnoticed clipping on a bright LCD
soft takes not caught until edit
acceptance_tests: exposure verified on a waveform or false color
critical focus verified with peaking or zoom

nodes.definition: Balance and stylize captured footage in post to achieve consistent, intentional color and contrast across shots.
contradictors: applies a random LUT and ships it

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reference look or capture color pipeline changes

pros.claim: grading unifies shots and sets the emotional tone
pros.example: matching two cameras' color makes a multicam seamless

cons.claim: grading cannot fully fix bad on-set exposure or white balance
cons.example: you cannot recover detail from clipped highlights

failure_modes: shots that do not match across a cut
over-graded skin that looks unnatural
acceptance_tests: shots match across the sequence on scopes
skin tones land on the natural skin-tone line

nodes.definition: Organize, sync, select, and assemble footage and audio into a coherent sequence with a reliable media workflow.
contradictors: edits from disorganized unsynced clips

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when footage organization or story structure changes

pros.claim: an organized, synced project makes editing fast and safe
pros.example: labeled selects let the editor find the best take instantly

cons.claim: disorganized media causes lost takes and sync errors
cons.example: unsynced audio drifts out across a long take

failure_modes: audio and video sync drift
lost or mislabeled takes
acceptance_tests: audio and video stay in sync across the cut
every take is organized and findable

nodes.definition: Plan and track shots, coverage, and continuity so the edit has every needed angle and consistent details.
contradictors: shoots with no list and hopes for coverage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when story structure or available shoot time changes

pros.claim: a shot list guarantees the edit has the coverage it needs
pros.example: listed inserts and cutaways give the editor options

cons.claim: missing coverage forces costly reshoots
cons.example: no cutaway means an unfixable jump cut

failure_modes: missing coverage discovered in the edit
continuity errors across takes
acceptance_tests: every scene has the coverage the edit needs
continuity details are tracked across takes

nodes.definition: Final quality check that exposure, focus, color, audio, and format meet the deliverable spec before release.
contradictors: exports and ships without a check

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when deliverable spec or platform requirements change

pros.claim: a final gate catches errors before they reach the audience
pros.example: QC flags clipped audio before publishing

cons.claim: skipping QC ships fixable defects to the audience
cons.example: a wrong aspect crop reaches the platform

failure_modes: defects shipped to the audience
wrong format or loudness for the platform
acceptance_tests: exposure, focus, color, and audio pass review
the export matches the platform spec

edges.why_related: the goal dictates the exposure look
edges.example: a bright corporate look versus a moody one
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before exposure

edges.why_related: framing intent drives lens choice
edges.example: a wide lens for a flattering portrait
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before the lens

edges.why_related: story emphasis shapes framing
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before framing

edges.why_related: mood intent shapes the key light
edges.risk_of_conflict: a key with no mood plan
edges.example: flat light for a dramatic brief
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before lighting

edges.why_related: the goal defines required coverage
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before the shot list

edges.why_related: the goal sets audio needs
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before audio

edges.why_related: the goal drives location needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a space with no criteria
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before location

edges.why_related: movement intent flows from the goal
edges.risk_of_conflict: moving the camera with no motivation
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before movement

edges.why_related: motion intent flows from the goal
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a rate with no intent
edges.resolution_rule: fix the goal before frame rate

edges.why_related: exposure baseline precedes color balance
edges.example: white balance set on a clipped frame
edges.resolution_rule: expose correctly before white balance

edges.why_related: aperture choice sets depth of field
edges.resolution_rule: decide aperture jointly for exposure and depth

edges.why_related: focal length affects depth of field
edges.example: wrong depth for the chosen length
edges.resolution_rule: pick the lens before the focus plan

edges.why_related: the lens determines available framing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: framing fits the field of view
edges.example: a frame impossible at that length
edges.resolution_rule: choose the lens before framing

edges.why_related: exposure target guides key intensity
edges.benefit_of_coupling: key set to the metered target
edges.resolution_rule: set the exposure target before the key

edges.why_related: the key defines the ratio reference
edges.resolution_rule: place the key before the fill

edges.why_related: the key and front plan precede the backlight
edges.example: a rim hotter than the key
edges.resolution_rule: place the key before the backlight

edges.why_related: the key source is shaped by modifiers
edges.resolution_rule: place the key before shaping it

edges.why_related: the key source temperature drives gel choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: gels reconcile the key to the look
edges.resolution_rule: place the key before gels

edges.why_related: white balance reference defines the target temperature for gels
edges.benefit_of_coupling: gels aim at the white balance reference
edges.example: gels fight the camera white balance
edges.resolution_rule: set white balance before gelling lights

edges.why_related: on-set white balance is the grading baseline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a clean baseline to grade from
edges.example: a grade fighting a bad cast
edges.resolution_rule: balance white balance on set before grading

edges.why_related: focus must be verified with tools
edges.example: soft takes missed on the LCD
edges.resolution_rule: verify focus with peaking and scopes

edges.why_related: exposure must be verified on scopes
edges.resolution_rule: verify exposure on a waveform

edges.why_related: verified exposure feeds a gradeable image
edges.resolution_rule: verify exposure before relying on the grade

edges.why_related: captured audio feeds the assembly
edges.resolution_rule: capture clean audio before assembly

edges.why_related: framed shots feed the assembly
edges.example: no usable frame to cut to
edges.resolution_rule: frame shots before assembly

edges.why_related: the grade must pass final QC
edges.resolution_rule: QC the grade before delivery

edges.why_related: the cut must pass final QC
edges.resolution_rule: QC the cut before delivery

edges.why_related: audio must pass final QC
edges.resolution_rule: QC audio before delivery

edges.why_related: coverage from the list enables assembly
edges.resolution_rule: plan coverage before relying on the edit

edges.why_related: the dressed space precedes lighting it
edges.benefit_of_coupling: light the space you actually have
edges.resolution_rule: control the location before lighting

edges.why_related: available light and an added key compete for the look
edges.risk_of_conflict: ambient overpowering the key or vice versa
edges.resolution_rule: let the dominant motivated source win and balance the other

edges.why_related: aperture for depth fights aperture for exposure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trade aperture against ISO and shutter
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing depth blows or starves exposure
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize the look then recover exposure with ISO, shutter, or ND

edges.why_related: fast movement and shutter cadence interact
edges.risk_of_conflict: a wrong shutter for the move judders
edges.example: a whip pan with a slow shutter smears
edges.resolution_rule: set shutter to match the planned movement

edges.why_related: heavy diffusion costs light and forces exposure changes
edges.example: a big softbox loses two stops
edges.resolution_rule: accept the exposure cost or move the light closer

edges.why_related: fill control and shaping daylight both manage shadow and ratio
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating a bounce with a lamp fill
edges.example: using a reflector as fill outdoors
edges.resolution_rule: treat reflector fill and lamp fill as the same ratio decision

edges.why_related: QC failures can send the shoot back to the goal
edges.risk_of_conflict: looping forever on minor QC notes
edges.example: a reshoot loop over a tiny flaw
edges.resolution_rule: stop when QC meets spec or risk is accepted, max two reshoot loops

edges.why_related: ungradeable color can trigger re-balancing on set
edges.resolution_rule: stop after white balance meets the reference, escalate if capture is the limit

edges.why_related: framing bounds where focus and depth can land
edges.example: a sharp background distracts from the subject
edges.resolution_rule: let composition constrain the depth-of-field choice

edges.why_related: the shot list bounds which moves are feasible in the time
edges.example: a complex move with no time to set up
edges.resolution_rule: constrain movement choices to the shot-list time budget

conflict_axes.trigger: opening the aperture for shallow depth over-exposes the image
resolution_order: pick the depth the look needs
recover exposure with ISO, shutter, or ND
verify on scopes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the intended look leads; exposure is recovered with neutral-density and ISO without changing the chosen aperture
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no ND or light control can hold both depth and exposure
conflict_axes.example: a shallow portrait outdoors needs an ND filter to avoid blowing the sky

conflict_axes.trigger: a strong ambient source competes with the intended key direction
resolution_order: identify the motivated dominant source
balance the secondary source to it
gel for temperature match
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the motivated source wins; the other is balanced in level and color rather than fought
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if ambient cannot be controlled and breaks the look
conflict_axes.example: a bright window forces using daylight as the key and gelling the lamps to match

conflict_axes.trigger: ambitious coverage and complex moves exceed the available shoot time
resolution_order: protect must-have coverage first
cut complex moves before essential angles
reschedule nice-to-haves
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: essential coverage the edit cannot live without dominates over optional camera moves
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if must-have coverage cannot fit the schedule
conflict_axes.example: dropping a gimbal sequence to guarantee the interview and cutaways are captured

conflict_axes.trigger: heavy diffusion for soft light loses the stops needed to expose
resolution_order: choose the needed softness
move the source closer or add power
accept ISO cost only if noise is acceptable
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the intended softness leads; output is regained by distance and power before raising ISO
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no light has enough power for the diffusion needed
conflict_axes.example: a big softbox needs a brighter lamp or to be moved in to hold exposure

conflict_axes.trigger: high frame rate for slow-motion forces a faster shutter that crisps motion
resolution_order: decide if slow-motion is required
match shutter to the base rate for normal cadence
accept crisper motion only for slow-mo shots
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the deliverable cadence leads; slow-motion is used only where it serves the story
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the look needs both natural blur and slow-motion in one shot
conflict_axes.example: shooting 120fps for a slow reveal but reverting to 24fps for dialogue

conflict_axes.trigger: filling shadows for safety flattens the dramatic modeling from the key
resolution_order: set the mood ratio from the brief
add only enough fill to retain needed detail
measure the ratio
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the mood intent dominates; fill is added only to the level the look allows
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if required shadow detail conflicts with the dramatic intent
conflict_axes.example: keeping a high-contrast ratio but lifting just enough fill to keep eyes visible

conflict_axes.trigger: getting the mic close enough competes with keeping it out of the frame
resolution_order: hide a lav or boom just out of frame
reframe slightly if needed
never sacrifice intelligible audio
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: intelligible audio dominates; framing yields a little before audio quality is sacrificed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no placement gives both clean audio and a clean frame
conflict_axes.example: choosing a hidden lav when a boom would dip into a wide shot

conflict_axes.trigger: relying on grading to fix exposure and color tempts skipping on-set verification
resolution_order: verify exposure and focus on set
grade only to enhance, not to rescue
escalate if capture is the limit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: on-set correctness dominates; grading enhances a good capture and cannot recover clipped or soft footage
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if footage is clipped, soft, or color-broken beyond grading
conflict_axes.example: refusing to over-expose on the promise of pulling highlights back in the grade

edge_cases.failure_mode: blown skies and skin with no detail
edge_cases.example: a white shirt clips to pure white
edge_cases.detection_method: check the waveform and false color for clipping
resolution: add ND or close the aperture

edge_cases.trigger: the subject's eyes are not critically sharp
edge_cases.example: focus sits on the ear not the eye
edge_cases.detection_method: zoom to 100 percent or use focus peaking on the eyes

edge_cases.trigger: mixed light sources split the frame into two color casts
edge_cases.failure_mode: a face lit half warm half cool
edge_cases.example: window daylight plus a tungsten lamp on one subject
edge_cases.detection_method: check a gray card and skin tone on a vectorscope
resolution: gel one source to match the other
kill or flag the rogue source
set white balance to the dominant source

edge_cases.trigger: shutter and light frequency mismatch causes rolling bands
edge_cases.example: banding under cheap LED panels at 1/50
edge_cases.detection_method: watch playback for moving bands at the working shutter
resolution: change shutter to a flicker-safe value
swap or dim the offending light

edge_cases.trigger: key on-axis or over-filled removes all modeling
edge_cases.example: a ring light killing all shadow
edge_cases.detection_method: check for shadow modeling on the subject's face

edge_cases.example: a loud laugh peaks the lav
edge_cases.detection_method: watch meters for peaks above the safe ceiling

edge_cases.trigger: the subject tone matches the background tone
edge_cases.failure_mode: the subject disappears into the background
edge_cases.example: dark hair against a dark wall
edge_cases.detection_method: check subject-to-background separation in the frame
resolution: add a rim or hair light

edge_cases.trigger: a needed angle or cutaway was never shot
edge_cases.example: no cutaway to hide a jump cut
edge_cases.detection_method: map every shot-list item to captured media before wrap

edge_cases.trigger: capture is clipped or color-broken beyond grading
edge_cases.failure_mode: shots that cannot be matched or recovered
edge_cases.example: trying to grade detail back into a clipped sky
edge_cases.detection_method: check scopes for clipping before committing to a grade
resolution: redesign the look around the footage

edge_cases.trigger: the master is exported and shipped without a final check
edge_cases.example: a wrong aspect crop published live
edge_cases.detection_method: require a QC pass against the spec before release

workflow.objective: fix the deliverable goal and the coverage needed to reach it
acceptance_tests: purpose names a viewer outcome
every scene has planned coverage
exit_criteria: goal, deliverable, and shot list fixed
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid unless the goal and coverage are fixed first

workflow.objective: choose and control the space and read its available light
acceptance_tests: background is clean or dressed
available light and acoustics are workable
workflow.do_first_because: camera and lighting choices depend on the space you actually have

workflow.objective: set the lens, exposure, and motion base for the look
acceptance_tests: no unintended clipping on the waveform
shutter is flicker-safe and matches the look
workflow.do_first_because: depth, focus, and lighting all build on the exposure and lens base

workflow.objective: build key, fill, backlight, quality, and color of the lighting
acceptance_tests: the key creates intended modeling
the ratio and color match the mood
workflow.do_first_because: lighting must be built before composition and focus are finalized on the lit subject

workflow.objective: compose the frame, set depth and focus, and balance white balance
acceptance_tests: framing follows a stated intent
the eyes are critically sharp
a gray card reads neutral
workflow.do_first_because: the framed, focused, balanced shot is what everything downstream records

workflow.objective: roll takes with stable support, clean audio, and verified exposure and focus
entry_criteria: composition, focus, and lighting locked for the shot
acceptance_tests: footage is stable and motivated
levels peak below clipping
exposure and focus verified on scopes
exit_criteria: all listed shots captured and verified
workflow.do_first_because: verified capture prevents discovering unusable takes only in the edit

workflow.objective: organize, sync, and assemble footage and audio into a cut

every take is findable

dominance_rules.trigger: clean audio competes with a clean frame
dominance_rules.rule: intelligible audio dominates over a marginally cleaner frame
dominance_rules.required_action: hide the mic just out of frame or reframe slightly before sacrificing audio
dominance_rules.example: choosing a hidden lav over a boom dipping into a wide

dominance_rules.trigger: a defect could be fixed on set or left for post
dominance_rules.rule: getting exposure, focus, and color right on set dominates over fixing in post
dominance_rules.required_action: verify on scopes and correct on set rather than relying on the grade
dominance_rules.example: re-exposing instead of promising to recover highlights later

dominance_rules.trigger: a faster shoot raises the risk of unusable footage
dominance_rules.rule: controlling risk of clipped, soft, or unsynced media dominates over shooting faster
dominance_rules.required_action: verify the high-risk shots before moving on
dominance_rules.example: checking focus on a hero shot even when behind schedule

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value step lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates over doing the most valuable step first
dominance_rules.required_action: complete prerequisites before the dependent step
dominance_rules.example: setting exposure before building the key light

dominance_rules.trigger: the master is ready to lock but QC has not passed
dominance_rules.rule: passing QC dominates over locking the deliverable
dominance_rules.required_action: run the QC checklist before any hard lock
dominance_rules.example: holding release until the loudness spec passes

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible delivery or high-risk choice is pending
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates over automated release for high-risk or irreversible steps
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off before release or reshoot decisions
dominance_rules.example: a human approves the master before publishing

dominance_rules.trigger: the convenient setting fights the intended look
dominance_rules.rule: the intended look dominates over a convenient default like auto exposure or white balance
dominance_rules.required_action: set manual values that serve the look and verify them
dominance_rules.example: manual white balance instead of auto under mixed light

dominance_rules.trigger: a metric looks precise but is only a heuristic estimate
dominance_rules.rule: correct evidence labeling dominates over the appearance of numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and do not imply measured data
dominance_rules.example: labeling estimated risk as heuristic not observed

dominance_rules.trigger: complex camera moves threaten essential coverage time
dominance_rules.rule: capturing essential coverage dominates over optional camera moves
dominance_rules.required_action: protect must-have angles before attempting elaborate moves
dominance_rules.example: dropping a gimbal sequence to secure the interview coverage

dominance_rules.trigger: a new object would lack a source or competency-question link
dominance_rules.rule: traceability dominates over creating objects with no source or question link
dominance_rules.required_action: link every node and edge to a source and a competency question
dominance_rules.example: every node references SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR and a CQ

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the goal and deliverable before any camera or light setup
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a setup for the wrong deliverable is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: settings change after the deliverable is clarified
anti_rework_rules.example: rigging lights before knowing the aspect ratio

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm every shot-list item is captured before wrapping
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the edit needs an angle that was never shot
anti_rework_rules.example: discovering no cutaway exists in the edit

anti_rework_rules.rule: control the location before lighting it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a location change forces relighting from scratch
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the lighting plan is rebuilt after moving locations
anti_rework_rules.example: lighting a corner then moving the subject across the room

anti_rework_rules.rationale: balancing color on a clipped frame is wasted work
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: white balance is redone after re-exposing
anti_rework_rules.example: setting white balance on an over-exposed frame

anti_rework_rules.rule: place the key before setting fill, backlight, and modifiers
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fill and ratio are meaningless without a key reference
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: fill is reset after the key is finally placed
anti_rework_rules.example: adding fill before deciding the key direction

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the lens before finalizing framing and focus
anti_rework_rules.rationale: framing planned for the wrong field of view is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the frame is re-planned after a lens swap
anti_rework_rules.example: planning a tight frame then mounting a wide lens

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify exposure and focus on scopes before moving to the next setup
anti_rework_rules.rationale: soft or clipped takes found in the edit require reshoots
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the edit reveals soft or clipped hero takes
anti_rework_rules.example: trusting the LCD then finding soft footage later

anti_rework_rules.rule: organize and sync the assembly before grading
anti_rework_rules.rationale: grading an unstable cut is redone when the cut changes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: grades are reapplied after the cut is reorganized
anti_rework_rules.example: grading before the cut is locked

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass QC before exporting and delivering the master
anti_rework_rules.rationale: shipping a defect forces a recall and re-delivery
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a defect is found after the master is published
anti_rework_rules.example: a wrong loudness level reaching the platform

anti_rework_rules.rule: require human review before committing to a reshoot or irreversible release
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unreviewed reshoot or release wastes time and budget
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a reshoot or release happens with no recorded review
anti_rework_rules.example: calling a reshoot over a flaw the client would accept

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a QC pass reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and QC notes to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and severity
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects are at the top
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue is empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the defective node
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map the defect type to a repair owner
acceptance_tests: each defect routed to one owner

iteration_protocol.detection: rerun the validator and affected acceptance tests
acceptance_tests: the previously failing checks now pass
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new information changes a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior shift to the revisit delta
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed from the formula
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior shift is below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
acceptance_tests: a decision record exists for each escalation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new version of the KB or look is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's checks and metrics
acceptance_tests: no unexplained regression remains
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all regressions are explained or fixed
